title: SIU clears cops in man's death
article: Two Barrie Police officers who shot and killed a man in July have been cleared of any wrongdoing.

Dennis Melton, 48, of Barrie was shot after a confrontation with two officers on Bayfield Street near the Kozlov Centre at 10:30 a.m. July 5. Melton was seen acting strangely on Bayfield Street, and when police approached, he stabbed both officers in the neck and throat area.
The first officer fired his gun, and the second officer started to follow Melton, ordering him to drop the knife. Melton ignored him and the officer shot a number of times.
Melton was taken to RVH and died from a series of gunshot wounds.
Both officers were also taken to hospital to be treated for their wounds. They were both released within a week.

The Special Investigations Unit was called to examine the events surrounding the death and, on Friday, Sept. 11, Const. Clayton Speers, 29, and Const. David Edgar, 26, were found not to have committed any crime.
SIU director Ian Scott said officers are allowed to use lethal force if someone is resisting arrest and could harm others, and there are no other alternatives.

"With respect to the issue of whether the flight could have been prevented in a less violent manner, it is worth noting that the officer did not have a Taser with him, and pepper spray would have been too risky in this circumstance of potentially imminent harm to others," said Scott.
"As well, the subject officer was justified under the self-defence section of the Criminal Code as he was under a reasonable apprehension that he would face imminent death or grievous bodily harm."
